waiver_statement: G9 INVERSION-INVARIANT fires on cross-category panel comparisons (sugar/satfat) because the BARI_PROTEIN_BAR_V1 lens explicitly reweights protein/fiber architecture as the primary scoring dimension. A higher-protein/higher-fiber bar can outrank a lower-sugar bar when sugar is below the red-label threshold (< 17.5g/100g). This is the intended behavior of the protein-bar sub-lens, not a scoring defect.

review.review_methodology: Manual pair-by-pair review: for each inversion pair, assessed whether the higher-scored product had meaningfully better protein density or fiber-to-sugar architecture per the lens's evaluative criteria, and whether the sugar/satfat disadvantage was below the Israeli red-label threshold.

conditions: Category caveat must disclose the protein-lens trade-off
Waiver must be re-reviewed if lens weights change materially (>5pp on protein/fiber dimensions)
Re-review required if corpus grows beyond 50 products

owner.context: TASK-399 tripwire-1 clearance (Nutrition APPROVE-WITH-CONDITIONS + Product GO)

governance_conditions: Applies ONLY when BARI_PROTEIN_BAR_V1 lens is active
If lens deactivated, G9 must re-run without waiver
Material scoring weight change (>5pp protein/fiber) requires re-review
Corpus > 50 products requires fresh 47-pair sample review
G9 gate still runs and is logged; this waiver makes the fire non-blocking for this category

gate_behavior.future_enhancement: Add --g9-waiver-ref GW-001 flag to run_gates.py to produce WAIVED status instead of FAIL

disclosure_requirement.content: The scoring lens rewards protein and fiber architecture; a high-protein/high-fiber bar can outrank a lower-sugar bar when sugar is below the red-label threshold. This is a deliberate design choice, not a general nutrition ranking.
